name: BN6's battle opening a frame longer
what: Every BN4 spec against BN6's (game=bn4:bn6) runs BN6's opening one paused frame longer, BN4's never and no BN5 spec: BN6's plain appear's first blink step counts 3 frames where it counts 2 (its movs r0,#2 at BN6_APPEAR_BLINK_FIRST made movs r0,#3, written into BN6's copy after the install: tools/xdiff_bn4.py alignments, the spec's first poke=). Its one object in the appear queue, the spec's virus, then runs its appear, and the paused present after it (XVirusFamily.present), as many times as BN4's does; the blink ends, the queue empties and bit 1 is set a frame later, so MegaMan's appear ends a frame later too (an object of the side the battle state names, its +0xD against the object's +0x16 at 0x080163C0-0x080163D4, skips the queue and the blink and waits for bit 1): the whole opening a frame longer, its fight frames counted as before. The tool checks BN6's ROM holds `was` there (a movs r0,#imm8) and writes its immediate plus `frames`; a spec of more than one foe is refused (the queue blinks its objects one after another, so a longer first blink step would delay the k-th foe k frames where BN4's bit delays each one)
why: The owner's call 7, revised (docs/multirom/bn4.md, The owner's calls): a BN4 visitor keeps BN6's appear and opening in play, and the comparison names the engines' frame between them, as it names BN6's battle a fight frame behind BN4's (allowed, lag 1). Both games' appears run the same steps (BN4_APPEAR 0x0800FE00, BN6_APPEAR 0x08016396, compared SAME by tools/xrecipe_thumb.py but for BN4's battle kind 0x44 and its sound): step 0 into the appear queue (BN4 0x08007F1C, BN6 0x0800AA1A), hidden, waiting for the battle state's appear bit 0 and the queue's head (BN4 0x080019C0 and 0x08007F04, BN6 0x0800139A and 0x0800AA06); step 1 a 2 x 16 frame blink, then out of the queue (BN4 0x08007F46, BN6 0x0800AA40); step 2 waiting for bit 1. Each opening sets bit 0 after its fade, from the same step (BN4 0x080E1F04: bl 0x08005B7C, bne; movs r0,#1; bl BN4_APPEAR_BITS_SET 0x080019A8 at 0x080E1F0E; BN6 0x080E1A04: bl 0x080062F8, bne; movs r0,#1; bl BN6_APPEAR_BITS_SET 0x08001382 at 0x080E1A0E; the fade begun with 0x10 in both, BN4 0x080E1EF4, BN6 0x080E19F4), 18 frames after the virus's init in BN4 (its step 0 run 19 times from its init's frame: frame 132 to 150 in spikey_v1, 131 to 149 in shrimpy_v3) and 17 in BN6 (17 runs from the frame after its init: 71 to 88), the blinks the same 32 frames: a probe of hooks on both, temporary, not kept (docs/rom/bn4.md, A virus's appear and the engine's appear bits). So BN4's virus runs its appear, and its after-state's sprite update, once more in the paused opening than BN6's: 53 after-states before its first fight frame against BN6's 51 and its state 1 (the battle's offset), its sprite a step ahead at t1, and Shrimpy's hook (0x080BA13E: its animation 1 cleared where the one in play has ended, 0x08002E56 bit 0x80) reading its idle animation's last frame a frame earlier, shrimpy_v3 FAIL at t65. The difference is the engines' openings, not the appear's code nor the family's. One paused run more of BN6's appear aligns it: a blink step a frame longer takes the run where a bit 0 a frame later would (the same count of appear runs, bit 1 a frame later), with one immediate of BN6's own appear and no code of the harness's; the bit itself a frame later would need a count the opening's step has not (0x080E1A04-0x080E1A16 sets it the frame the fade ends)
evidence: python3 tools/xdiff.py shrimpy_v3 --poke 080163FC:2003:2 (BN6's first blink step a frame longer) PASS, the opening's allowance then in legit.json unused; without it FAIL at t65 (2026-11-04)

with the alignment every BN4 spec against BN6's PASSES and the opening's allowance and its code (tools/xdiff_bn4.py opening_animation, OPENING_LEAD, anim_steps) are gone; its mutation (tests/xdiff/mutations.json, shrimpy_v3: the first blink step 4 frames, the alignment two) is caught
